item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 271752
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Thu Aug 27 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll.

Central East Pacific (EP93):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a low pressure system
located about 900 miles south of the southern tip of the Baja
California peninsula are showing better signs of organization.
Recent satellite-derived wind data indicate that this system is
already producing winds of tropical-storm-force. If current trends
continue, advisories will be initiated on a tropical storm this
afternoon. This system is forecast to move generally northwestward
at 10 to 15 mph for the next several days, staying well offshore of
the coast of Mexico. For additional information on this system,
including Gale Warnings, please see the High Seas Forecast issued
by the National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...near 100 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...near 100 percent.

Western East Pacific (EP94):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a low pressure area
located well east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands have continued
to become better organized. Environmental conditions appear
conducive for continued development, and a tropical depression is
likely to form within the next day or so while the system drifts to
the northeast, before turning westward this weekend.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form this weekend well to the
south of southwestern Mexico. Environmental conditions appear
favorable for gradual development of this system, and a tropical
depression is likely to form early next week while it moves
west-northwestward to northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands over the weekend or early next week. Some gradual
development is possible thereafter while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward, well offshore of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Zelinsky/Evans/Pierce

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Karina Advisory Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
200 PM MST Thu Aug 27 2026
 
...TROPICAL STORM KARINA FORMS WELL OFFSHORE THE COAST OF 
SOUTHWEST MEXICO...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...11.1N 111.9W
ABOUT 825 MI...1330 KM S OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 295 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1001 MB...29.56 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Karina was
located near latitude 11.1 North, longitude 111.9 West. Karina is
moving toward the west-northwest near 13 mph (20 km/h) and this
general motion is expected to continue over the next several days. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts.
Strengthening is anticipated, and Karina is forecast to become a 
hurricane over the weekend. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles (335 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1001 mb (29.56 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Tropical Storm Karina will begin to 
affect portions of the coast of southwest Mexico and the Baja 
California Peninsula this weekend.  These swells are likely to cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.  Please consult 
products from your local weather office.

 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Pierce/Zelinsky

item.title: Tropical Storm Karina Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 272046
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Karina Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
200 PM MST Thu Aug 27 2026

Satellite imagery indicates that the area of low pressure (Invest 
EP93) has developed a more organized circulation, along with banded 
convection around its center. The most recent subjective Dvorak 
analysis from TAFB was 2.5/2.5, which reflects this organization. 
Scatterometry data from around 1600 UTC also showed a slightly 
elongated, but closed circulation with max winds between 35 and 40 
kt. Based on this, advisories have been initiated on Tropical Storm 
Karina, with an initial intensity of 40 kt. 

The initial motion estimate was set at 295/11 kt. Karina is expected 
to continue on a northwestward track over the next several days, 
staying well off the coast of Mexico. A high pressure ridge centered 
over the southwestern US will drive Karina's northwestward motion, 
before an upper-level trough just off the Pacific coast is forecast 
to shift Karina's track more westward around early next week. 
Forecast models are in good agreement through 72 h on Karina's 
track, then show more spread as the cyclone moves away from the 
ridge's influence, thus hindering forecast confidence heading into 
next week.

SHIPS guidance suggests a favorable environment for strengthening 
over the next several days as Karina moves over warm SSTs in a 
moisture-rich, low vertical wind shear environment. Models depict a 
steady intensification period over the next 72 h, before moving into 
an environment of cooler SSTs and reduced mid-level moisture. The 
SHIPS-RII consensus guidance suggests a nearly 50 percent chance of 
a 55 kt increase in winds in the next 48 hours, indicating that 
strengthening could occur at a faster rate. However, given that the 
storm currently lacks a tight inner core, the initial forecast 
reflects a slower intensification rate, and has generally followed 
the HCCA for both track and intensity.

item.title: Tropical Storm Lowell Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 272046
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Lowell Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP122026
1100 AM HST Thu Aug 27 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that the disturbance well to the 
west-southwest of the Baja California Peninsula and well 
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands has developed well-organized 
convective bands. Recently received ASCAT data showed a closed 
circulation which, while elongated NE-SW, was producing winds near 
35 kt about 50 n mi southeast of the center.  Based on this, 
advisories are initiated on Tropical Storm Lowell.

The initial motion is a somewhat uncertain 065/4 kt.  During the 
next day or two, Lowell is expected to turn westward as a low- to 
mid-level ridge builds to the north.  A generally westward motion 
should continue for the rest of the forecast period. The guidance 
has some spread in the forward speed by 120 h, which seems to be 
due to possible effects on the steering flow by the larger Tropical 
Storm Karina to the east. The forecast track is near the center of 
the guidance envelope and splits the speed difference between the 
models.

Lowell will be over warm sea surface temperatures during the next 
five days and in an environment of light to moderate easterly 
shear. This should allow steady strengthening, and the initial 
intensity forecast is near the center of the intensity guidance.  
Since the environment is favorable and some of the guidance is 
stronger than the current forecast, it is possible that Lowell will 
strengthen more and faster than currently forecast.
